transcript: Mamma Mia is coming back to Broadway, and, uh, I'm kind of conflicted. On one hand, I love Mamma Mia. I think it's a really fun show, and I'm genuinely excited to see it back on Broadway. But on the other hand, it does feel like another show in this trend of let's bring a touring show and plop it on a Broadway stage for a limited engagement. Obviously, we saw it last season, notably with the Wiz. There's a rumor that we may be seeing this with the Beetlejuice tour as well. And it does feel like this is something that's going to come more and more common whether we like it or not. And maybe this is the latest of me to say, but it does feel like it is cheapening the Broadway experience a little bit. Because touring sets are not custom built for Broadway stages. They are designed to be able to be put up and taken down as quickly as possible and fit in the back of a couple of trucks. They are often scaled back in terms of production quality and also have a lot of limitations, like they don't have elevator lifts. They don't have on stage automations that you typically get on a Broadway show. And so, while Broadway tours are a great way to make theater more accessible to people around the country who may not be able to get to New York, when you compare your average touring production to a Broadway production, they are inferior in a lot of ways by design. You're trading that quality for portability. And if you're going to be charging Broadway prices, I feel like you should be getting a Broadway quality production. And yes, I realize that Broadway touring prices have gone insane over the past couple of years, in some cases even being more expensive than Broadway. That is a whole other topic for a whole other video. When it comes to just the notion of putting a touring show on a Broadway stage, I don't know. I find it to be a troubling trend. That being said, the one positive about this model is the fact that you are taking this touring cast and giving them the opportunity to perform on Broadway and get a Broadway credit. Because oftentimes, touring cast are just as talented as the people that you see on Broadway. They just may not have as many credits to their name. And so giving them that opportunity, I think, is a really good thing. I just wish they had an actual Broadway production around them rather than one that was designed to tour.
